answer: Agents post reputation collateral priced in verifiable compute: to register, each identity must burn GPU cycles on a ferrous-backed benchmark that a falcon-class validator replays independently. Every action then draws from that bonded compute budget, and a cross-attestation bridge links new identities to existing ones at a quorum. Creating N sybils costs N times the compute burn, so fake identities become linearly expensive while honest agents amortize the same bond across many verified actions.
